subject: Post-call follow-up: sensitive field storage & logging commitments
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Megan Lowe <megan.lowe@datacare.io>, procurement@datacare.io
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps (sensitive-field handling)

Hi Megan — thanks for taking time earlier. Quick recap and the asks we captured on the call so we’re aligned: 

1) Scope of sensitive fields: you mentioned two categories — direct patient identifiers (name, DOB, SSN) and device serials that tie back to patients. Confirmed these are the only fields you consider PII for the initial pilot.
2) Storage desire: DataCare needs confirmation that prompt inputs containing PII are not persisted to long-term storage by default.
3) Logging: you need audit logs of inference requests (timestamps + model version + request id) but redacted of raw prompt text for PII-bearing requests.
4) Residency: pilot must keep all persistent artifacts in us-west-2.
5) Retention windows: you requested 30 days for request-level telemetry and 90 days for aggregated metrics.

Next steps we agreed: Redwood will confirm exactly what we retain by default, show available redaction options, and provide SOC2 evidence + a short diagram of the dataflow for PII requests.

I’m looping in Rachel (security lead for the deal) and Aditya (solutions) to provide the confirmation items. Rachel/Aditya — could you please confirm the bullets below and attach the SOC2 summary + dataflow diagram?

• Default retention for prompt inputs/outputs (pilot)
• Options to disable storage of prompt text entirely or keep only hashed identifiers
• Logging format for audit trail (can we provide request id + timestamp without prompt text?)
• Residency controls available for hosted vs dedicated

Thanks all — I’ll hold on sending procurement milestone items until we confirm the above.

Best,
Ben
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

From: Megan Lowe <megan.lowe@datacare.io>

Cc: procurement@datacare.io, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 17:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps (sensitive-field handling)

Thanks Ben — that captures it well. A couple clarifications from our side before you send the formal confirmation: 

• When you say "not persisted to long-term storage by default" — can you spell out what "by default" means for hosted customers vs dedicated pools? We will evaluate hosted but may require dedicated for production.
• Redaction: we need the ability to configure rule-based redaction (pattern + field name) at ingestion time, not only at downstream logs.
• Retention for audit logs: 30 days raw request metadata ok, but we may need a mechanism to export to our archival store before deletion.

If you can include an example audit log row (fields we’d see) and the simple dataflow image that shows the redaction step, that will help us close the security questionnaire.

— Megan
VP Product, DataCare

On a related note, procurement asked whether there are any fees to enable residency in us-west-2 or to switch to dedicated capacity; can someone include that in the pricing note?

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Megan Lowe <megan.lowe@datacare.io>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps (sensitive-field handling)

Megan — thanks for the clarifying questions. Below are concrete confirmations and options. I’ve attached a short SOC 2 summary and a one-page dataflow diagram that highlights the redaction step. Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, sensitive-field-dataflow.png, retention-policy-snippet.txt

1) "By default": Hosted API (standard) — transient in-memory request buffers only; prompt text is kept in unstable cache for up to 2 hours for streaming/backpressure recovery and then dropped. No prompt text is written to durable object storage or analytics pipelines unless customer enables logging.

Dedicated pools — similar transient behavior, with the option to configure a persistent logging sink. For pilots where customers request no persistent prompt storage we can enforce a policy that prevents writing prompt text to any disk-backed store.

2) Redaction at ingestion: Redwood supports configurable ingestion hooks that apply rule-based redaction (regex or field mapping) at the edge before the request reaches the runtime. This is available as a tenant-level toggle today and can be scoped per-route. We’ll provide a short example configuration if helpful.

3) Audit log format and retention: Example audit row we can provide: {timestamp, request_id, model_id, route, user_tenant_id, response_status, token_count}.

Importantly, the audit row can omit prompt_text/payload fields for PII-marked routes; we can also write a hashed identifier only (SHA-256) to link logs to your internal records. Default retention windows: raw request metadata 30 days; aggregated metrics 90 days. Exports: we support S3 export hooks and can push raw metadata to a customer S3 in us-west-2 before deletion on a scheduled cadence.

4) Residency controls & fees: Residency to us-west-2 is supported on both Hosted and Dedicated. There is no additional fee for regional placement during pilot proof-of-concept. Pricing for dedicated capacity and guaranteed residency in production is part of the reserved-capacity quote; Ben will follow up with exact pricing bands and any uplift.

Next steps I will take today:
• Attach SOC2 summary + dataflow diagram (below).
• Draft a short sample ingestion configuration and an audit-log example file.
• Confirm export cadence options for S3 (daily, hourly).

If this matches your needs I can prepare a short note you can include in the security questionnaire.

—Rachel
Director, Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference
